blocks.text: A garage door arm, a pendulum-clock bar and a wheel rolling off a loading ramp all obey the same three equations. Before releasing the bar on a test rig, an engineer wants to know how fast it will start to swing and what the pin must carry. The free-body diagram and three equations give both answers.

blocks.markdown: For a rigid body in plane motion, Newton's laws reduce to three scalar equations. The first two relate the net external force to the acceleration of the centre of mass G, and the third relates the net moment about G to the angular acceleration. Here $m$ is mass in kg, $\mathbf a_G$ is in m/s$^2$, $I_G$ is the moment of inertia about the axis through G in kg m$^2$ and $\alpha$ is in rad/s$^2$.

blocks.caption: The three planar equations of motion, with moments taken about the centre of mass.

blocks.title: Fixed-axis rotation
blocks.text: For a body pivoted at a fixed point O, moments may be taken about O instead: $\sum M_O=I_O\alpha$, with $I_O$ the moment of inertia about O. The centre of mass moves on a circle of radius $e=OG$, so $a_{Gt}=e\alpha$ (tangential) and $a_{Gn}=e\omega^2$ (toward O).

blocks.markdown: **Method.** Draw the body alone and show every external force (weight $mg$ at G, normal forces, friction, pin reactions) and any moments. Choose axes, write the three equations, and add kinematic relations if there are more unknowns than equations. Count unknowns before solving.

blocks.title: Bar released from rest
blocks.prompt: A uniform bar (mass 3 kg, length 1.2 m) is pinned at one end O and released from rest in the horizontal position. Find the initial angular acceleration and the pin reaction. Use $g=9.81$ m/s$^2$.

steps.text: Moments about O, with $I_O=\tfrac13mL^2=1.44$ kg m$^2$. Only the weight (arm $L/2=0.6$ m) has a moment, and $\omega=0$ at release.
The centre of mass accelerates downward at $a_G=0.6\alpha=7.36$ m/s$^2$ and $\omega=0$ so there is no normal acceleration. Vertical equation:
Horizontal equation: no horizontal acceleration at release.

blocks.answer: $\alpha=12.26$ rad/s$^2$ (clockwise as drawn), $O_y=7.36$ N upward and $O_x=0$. The pin carries only $mg/4$ at release.

blocks.markdown: **Rolling down an incline.** A body of mass $m$ and radius $R$ with $I_G=mk^2$ (where $k$ is the radius of gyration in m) rolls without slip down an incline of angle $\theta$. Take $x$ down the slope. Friction $F$ acts up the slope at the contact point. Then $mg\sin\theta-F=ma$, $N=mg\cos\theta$ and $FR=I_G\alpha$ with the rolling constraint $a=R\alpha$.

blocks.title: Minimum friction for a cylinder
blocks.prompt: A solid cylinder (mass 10 kg, $k^2/R^2=\tfrac12$) rolls without slip down a $30^\circ$ incline. Find $a$, $F$ and the minimum $\mu_s$.

blocks.caption: Rolling down an incline without slip (all independent of mass and radius).

blocks.title: Mass distribution matters
blocks.text: The more of the mass lies near the rim (larger $k^2/R^2$), the slower the body accelerates and the more friction it needs. A sphere beats a cylinder, which beats a hoop.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.text: Using $I_G$ with moments about the pin (use $I_O$), assuming $F=\mu N$ when the body rolls without slip, and forgetting that the centre of mass of a pivoted bar has a normal acceleration $e\omega^2$ once it is moving.

items: Draw the FBD, write three equations, add the constraint.
Pivoted body: use $\sum M_O=I_O\alpha$ to find $\alpha$ first, then force equations for the pin.

points: The planar equations are $\sum F_x=ma_{Gx}$, $\sum F_y=ma_{Gy}$, $\sum M_G=I_G\alpha$.
A bar pinned at one end and released horizontally has $\alpha=3g/(2L)$.
Rolling without slip needs $\mu_s\ge\frac{k^2/R^2}{1+k^2/R^2}\tan\theta$, e.g. $\tfrac13\tan\theta$ for a solid cylinder.

questions.stem: Which set of equations correctly describes the general plane motion of a rigid body of mass $m$ and centroidal inertia $I_G$?

distractorRationale.b: These are equilibrium equations and are valid only if the accelerations are zero.
distractorRationale.c: The rotational equation needs the moment of inertia, not the mass.
distractorRationale.d: This mixes up force and moment equations.

questions.explanation: The planar equations of motion equate the net force to $m\mathbf a_G$ and the net moment about G to $I_G\alpha$. Equilibrium is the special case where all accelerations vanish.

questions.stem: A uniform bar of length 0.90 m is pinned at one end and released from rest in the horizontal position. Using $g=9.81$ m/s$^2$, what is its initial angular acceleration?

distractorRationale.a: This uses $I_G=\tfrac1{12}mL^2$ with the pin moment, instead of $I_O=\tfrac13mL^2$.
distractorRationale.c: This is $g/L$, ignoring the factors from $mg(L/2)$ and $I_O$.
distractorRationale.d: This confuses $\alpha$ with the free-fall acceleration $g$.

questions.explanation: At release $\omega=0$, so $mg(L/2)=\tfrac13mL^2\alpha$ and $\alpha=3g/(2L)=3(9.81)/1.8=16.35$ rad/s$^2$. The mass cancels.

questions.stem: A uniform bar of length 1.5 m is pinned at one end and released from rest when it makes $30^\circ$ with the horizontal (above it). Using $g=9.81$ m/s$^2$, find its initial angular acceleration in rad/s$^2$.
questions.explanation: The weight's moment arm about the pin is $(L/2)\cos30^\circ$, so $mg(L/2)\cos30^\circ=\tfrac13mL^2\alpha$. Hence $\alpha=\frac{3g\cos30^\circ}{2L}=\frac{3(9.81)(0.866)}{3.0}=8.50$ rad/s$^2$.

questions.stem: A thin hoop rolls without slipping down a $25^\circ$ incline. Find the minimum coefficient of static friction required (dimensionless).
questions.explanation: For a hoop $k^2/R^2=1$, so $\mu_{s,\min}=\tfrac12\tan\theta=0.5\tan25^\circ=0.233$. Friction needed is $\tfrac12mg\sin\theta$ while the normal force is $mg\cos\theta$.

questions.stem: A solid sphere ($I_G=\tfrac25mR^2$) rolls without slip down a $20^\circ$ incline. What is the minimum coefficient of static friction?

distractorRationale.b: This is $\tfrac13\tan20^\circ$, the value for a solid cylinder.
distractorRationale.c: This is $\tan20^\circ\times0.5$, the value for a hoop.
distractorRationale.d: This is $\tan20^\circ$, the value for a block to start sliding, ignoring rolling.

questions.explanation: For a sphere $k^2/R^2=\tfrac25$ so $\mu_{s,\min}=\frac{2/5}{7/5}\tan\theta=\tfrac27\tan20^\circ=0.104$. The sphere needs less friction than a cylinder or hoop because less of its mass is far from the axis.

questions.stem: A uniform bar is pinned at O and swings. An engineer wants $\alpha$ directly from a single moment equation, avoiding the unknown pin reactions. Which equation should be used?

distractorRationale.a: The centroidal inertia applies only with moments about G.
distractorRationale.b: The bar accelerates, so the forces do not balance.
distractorRationale.c: The net moment about G is $I_G\alpha$, which is not zero while the bar angularly accelerates.

questions.explanation: For fixed-axis rotation, moments about the pin eliminate both pin force components, and $\sum M_O=I_O\alpha$ holds with the inertia about the same axis. Using $I_G$ with $M_O$ is a frequent error.

questions.stem: A uniform rod (mass 6 kg, length 2.0 m) lies on a smooth horizontal table (no friction). A horizontal force of 12 N is applied perpendicular to the rod at one end. Find the rod's angular acceleration in rad/s$^2$ (use $I_G=\tfrac1{12}mL^2$).
questions.explanation: Moments about G (no other horizontal forces): $P(L/2)=I_G\alpha$, so $\alpha=\frac{12(1.0)}{\tfrac{1}{12}(6)(4)}=\frac{12}{2}=6.0$ rad/s$^2$. The centre also accelerates at $P/m=2$ m/s$^2$.

questions.stem: A uniform bar (mass 5 kg, length 2.4 m) is pinned at one end and released from rest in the horizontal position. Find the vertical pin reaction in N at the instant of release (take $g=9.81$ m/s$^2$).
questions.explanation: Initially $\alpha=3g/(2L)$, so $a_G=(L/2)\alpha=\tfrac34g=7.36$ m/s$^2$ downward and $\omega=0$. Then $mg-O_y=ma_G$ gives $O_y=mg/4=12.26$ N upward.

questions.stem: A uniform solid cylinder rolls without slipping down a rough incline of angle $\theta$. Draw (describe) its free-body diagram and write the three equations of motion with the rolling constraint, defining all symbols.
markingGuide: Lists forces: weight $mg$ at G, normal force $N$ perpendicular to the incline, and friction $F$ up the slope at the contact point
questions.explanation: Four unknowns ($a$, $\alpha$, $F$, $N$) are matched by three equations plus the rolling constraint. The no-slip assumption is valid only if $F/N\le\mu_s$.

questions.stem: Derive the minimum static friction coefficient needed for a uniform solid cylinder to roll without slipping down an incline of angle $\theta$, and explain what happens if the actual coefficient is smaller.
markingGuide: If $\mu_s$ is smaller, the cylinder slips while rolling; kinetic friction $\mu_kN$ applies and the constraint $a=R\alpha$ no longer holds
questions.explanation: The result is independent of mass and radius. A slipping cylinder has $a>R\alpha$ because the contact point slides down the slope relative to the surface.
